title: Пропавшее филе ягнёнка  (The Missing Lamb Fillet)

segments.t: Back in the kitchen, Fedya warns Senya that he is stealing food right in front of everyone. Moments later, Lyova notices a missing lamb fillet. Listen to the full conversation in Russian first, and then we will walk through every line together.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.

'You are already stealing in front of everyone.' Once Lyova is already stealing in front of everyone, Fedya can finally tell Lyova what he means. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'And what if they catch you right now?' With the work and kitchen hanging in the air, Fedya puts Lyova on the spot.
'I steal from the rich and give to the poor.' Admitting that he steals from the rich and give to the poor shows Senya being honest for a change.
'That is, you give it only to yourself.' Since that is Lyova gives it only to themselves, Fedya does not waste words on excuses.
'Alright, and where is the lamb fillet?' Wondering if Alright and where is the lamb fillet shows Lyova caught off guard.
'Senya, have you not seen it?' Here checking whether Fedya not seen it shows Lyova looking for the real truth. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'Why is Senya immediately to blame?' By asking why Senya immediately to blame is, Senya presses Fedya for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'I have not seen any fillet.' By having not seen any fillet, Senya keeps his side of the story grounded.
'And why are you so nervous?' Asking why Fedya so nervous is is how Lyova puts Fedya on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'I am not nervous at all.' Here being not nervous at all sets up the next turn in their exchange.
'Why do you suspect me?' By wondering why Fedya suspect him, Senya presses Fedya for a straight answer.

'Have you caught me even once?' Asking whether Fedya caught him even once cuts straight through the tension between Senya and Fedya. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'I am forced to search you.' Once he is forced to search Fedya, Lyova can finally tell Fedya what he means. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Senya acts outraged, yet agrees to let Lyova search his pockets right there in the kitchen. Watch how Senya hides the stolen food. Until next time!
